title: Htipiti
subtitle: Greek whipped feta and roasted red pepper dip
excerpt: Feta cheese beaten with roasted red pepper, olive oil and a little chilli into a creamy, salty, smoky dip. Ready in 10 minutes and keeps well for days in the fridge.
sourceNotes: Northern Greek meze tradition, particularly associated with Thessaly and Macedonia.

recipe.batchNotes: Double the batch and store in jars. Keeps for up to five days refrigerated.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make up to three days ahead. The flavour deepens as it rests. Drizzle fresh olive oil on top before serving.

content.text: Htipiti is a beaten dip of feta and roasted red pepper. The pepper needs to be properly charred for the smoky depth to come through. Blend until smooth and adjust the chilli to your liking.
Place the whole red peppers directly over a gas flame or under a hot grill. Char them on all sides until the skin is black. This takes about 15 to 20 minutes.
Place the charred peppers in a bowl and cover tightly with cling film. Leave for 10 minutes. The steam loosens the skin.
Peel the peppers under cold running water. Remove the seeds and stalks. Pat dry with kitchen paper.
Put the feta, roasted pepper flesh, olive oil, chilli flakes and lemon juice in the blender.
Blend until smooth. Add the yoghurt and garlic if using. Blend again for 30 seconds.
Taste for salt and chilli. Feta is salty so you may need none. Add black pepper and blend briefly.
Spoon into a bowl. Drizzle with olive oil and add a pinch of chilli flakes. Serve with pitta or bread.

items.cause: Feta varies widely in salt content.
items.fix: Stir in extra yoghurt or a spoonful of cream cheese to dilute the saltiness.

items.symptom: The dip is grainy, not smooth.
items.cause: The feta was not blended long enough, or the peppers were not fully peeled.
items.fix: Blend for a further minute and scrape down the sides of the jug.

items.cause: The peppers were roasted rather than charred over an open flame.
items.fix: Add a pinch of smoked paprika to the blender to compensate.
